subject: Model fine-tune ban and EU-only routing for HealthSync
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@healthsync.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Model fine-tune ban and routing for HealthSync

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the call this morning. A couple of follow-ups from our legal and procurement teams:

1) HealthSync needs an explicit contractual commitment that our customer data will not be used to fine-tune or otherwise improve public or internal models (no fine-tuning/no training).
2) All inference and any associated telemetry must be processed and stored only within EU data centers (EU-only routing).
3) We need a subprocessor map and SOC2 + any recent penetration test report to attach to our procurement packet.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Add a DPA amendment that includes the no-fine-tune clause and a retention routing clause?
- Provide a list of subprocessors and the latest SOC2 Type II report (or a link) for procurement?

Procurement has a DocuSign flow ready but they want the DPA redline returned before routing for signature.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Security and Compliance
HealthSync

Attachments: none

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@healthsync.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 12:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Model fine-tune ban and routing for HealthSync

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes to a DPA amendment with a no-fine-tune/no-training commitment, and yes to EU-only inference routing for your production traffic (we have options for hosted EU zones and a Private VPC deployment).

Next steps I propose:
- I attached a checklist we need to fill (subprocessor_map.csv) so I can pass to infra + security.
- Marissa (legal) has been looped in to prepare the DPA redline; she can confirm exact language and any narrowly scoped telemetry carve-outs.
- I'll request SOC2 docs from security and share the link or an NDA'd package if procurement prefers.

Would you prefer the EU-only routing scoped as an operational routing rule (per-route vs account-level) or as a contract-level commitment that we enforce for the HealthSync account? We can do both; contract-level gives you clearer assurances for audits.

Proposed immediate action items:
1) Elena: confirm routing scope (per-route vs account-level) and whether telemetry masking is acceptable for logs.
2) HealthSync procurement: send the Docusign packet when you have the redline returned.
3) Logan -> Security: assemble SOC2 + pen test references and attach to thread.

Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: subprocessor_map.csv (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@healthsync.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Model fine-tune ban and routing for HealthSync

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear checklist. I pulled together a short redline and a suggested amendment text to insert into the DPA; key points are below (I've attached the full redline doc as DPA_redline_v2.docx):

- No-Training Commitment: Redwood will not use HealthSync account inputs or outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve any models used in Redwood-hosted inference, except for ephemeral telemetry used solely for service health (latency/error rates) that is aggregated and cannot be attributed to HealthSync customers.

- Export and Routing: Redwood will commit in the amendment to process HealthSync production inference traffic within EU data centers and will not transfer production request bodies or inference outputs outside the EU unless directed by HealthSync in writing.

- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide a subprocessor map as an attachment (we will maintain this as a living list).

- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report and recent pen-test summary will be provided under NDA; can be linked from a secure drive or transmitted via your procurement portal.

A couple of notes:
- The no-training commitment covers model improvement activities; we typically reserve the right to use aggregated, de-identified metrics for product improvement. I've tried to capture that balance in the redline; if HealthSync needs a blanket exclusion, we can tighten the language but must document the operational impact (e.g., limits to certain telemetry-based alerts).
- For EU-only routing, if you require absolute legal guarantee (e.g., for regulatory audit), we recommend opting for a Private VPC deployment with regionally pinned control plane—I'll outline costs in a separate note.

Please review the redline and let us know any edits; if procurement needs the DocuSign flow, we can return a signed amendment as soon as it's agreed.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_redline_v2.docx (redline of DPA)

From: Elena Morales <elena@healthsync.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@healthsync.ai
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 15:06:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Model fine-tune ban and routing for HealthSync

Marissa / Logan —

Thanks, the redline looks like the right direction. A few follow-ups from procurement/security:

- Procurement wants the SOC2 Type II report or an access link so they can attach it to the purchase order. It must be accessible by our vendor risk team by EOD Friday.
- Security asks for a narrow definition of "ephemeral telemetry" used for service health. Can you provide two short example categories that will be retained (e.g., aggregated latency percentiles, anonymized error classes) and state retention windows?
- For routing: we will take your recommendation and request the Private VPC (EU pinned) option for production. Please also provide an estimated delta in monthly cost for the VPC option vs hosted EU.

Once procurement has the redline and SOC2 link, they'll send DocuSign. Attached is our standard vendor questionnaire and the procurement form (healthsync_procurement_form.pdf) — please fill and return if possible.

Best,
Elena

Attachment: healthsync_procurement_form.pdf (procurement questionnaire)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@healthsync.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 16:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Model fine-tune ban and routing for HealthSync

Elena —

Quick updates and links:

1) SOC2: Shared a secure link to the SOC 2 Type II package here: https://drive.redwood.internal/healthsync/soc2-2026 (procurement should have access; if not, we can deliver via your vendor portal under NDA).

2) Telemetry examples & retention:
   - Aggregated latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for production routes — retained 90 days.
   - Anonymized error class counts (e.g., 4xx vs 5xx buckets) — retained 30 days.
   - No raw request/response payloads will be retained for training.

3) Private VPC cost delta: estimated +40% monthly over standard hosted EU plan for reserved capacity (depends on GPU profile and throughput). Karthik will follow up with an accurate quote and sizing options.

4) DocuSign: Procurement link prepared — https://docusign.com/hs/HS-4552-sign (this will include the DPA amendment once redline is finalized).

Next steps: Karthik will send the VPC quote; Marissa will incorporate any remaining edits into the redline and we can route DocuSign. I'll also fill the procurement form and return it by EOD Monday.

Thanks all — looking forward to closing this.

Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments shared in thread: subprocessor_map.csv, DPA_redline_v2.docx, healthsync_procurement_form.pdf
